Explicit mathematical counterexample to the identified reading (not Lean-compiled): K=1, Ω=([-2,-1]∪[1,2])×[-1,1] with normalized product Lebesgue law, X the first coordinate, Y the second, interpreted as a one-coordinate vector. Marginal f=1/2 on the closed two-interval set and zero elsewhere; joint density q=1/4 on its product with [-1,1] and zero elsewhere. These densities are nonnegative, integrable, normalize to one, and range(X)={f>0} exactly including endpoints. Coordinates and Y are bounded measurable and E[X]=0. Independence and symmetric Y give the CEF zero. Both m0=0 and m1(x)=x(1-x²)² for |x|<1, zero otherwise, are globally differentiable and zero on the entire X range. At ±1 the polynomial and its first derivative vanish, so the extension is C1. Thus both are genuine conditional means for the identical joint law, with derivatives at zero 0 and 1. The mean lies in the support gap; no null-set interior artifact or undefined integral. For the second conjunct, n=1 and mhat identically zero give positive sample size and differentiability, and the equality is reflexive. This witness tests distributional uniqueness, not the derivative of a fixed chosen extension.

Explicit mathematical counterexample (not Lean-compiled): n=1, y0=1>0. For every s>0 use θ=(1,0,1,s,0,1,1), a valid mixture consisting of a proper normal density at mean 1 with positive scale s; unused component scales and rate remain positive. Its likelihood is 1/(s sqrt(2π)), unbounded as s decreases to zero. Every fixed valid parameter has finite likelihood, so none is a maximizer. The witness satisfies the canonical printed reading: positive sample size, ordinary positive observation, valid nonnegative normalized mixture weights, real locations, positive scales/rate, and the iid sampling context (one observation, or any ordinary continuous model containing y=1 in its support). This negates universal existence (A) without using any density junk value.

Explicit mathematical counterexample (not Lean-compiled): put s_k=2^(-(k+1)), p_k=1/(k+2), t_k=s_k p_k, c_k=s_k(1-p_k), k∈ℕ. Both conditional-arm PMF-positive supports are all ℕ (or its embedding in ℝ), and the propensity ratio is p_k. Since p_k tends to zero, no common ε>0 works. This witness has uniform positivity failure and equal supports, so directly contradicts B under ordinary countable probability, not merely a guessed support condition for hedged C. In the same mass domain the forward direction A holds algebraically, so the negated equivalence cannot be witnessed only by a failure of A.

Explicit mathematical nondegenerate PDF instance: X uniform on [-1,1], Z an independent fair Rademacher, Y=X²+Z, on the product of the closed interval and two atoms. f=1/2 on [-1,1], zero elsewhere, is a legitimate density including endpoint version values, and the range equals this interval. The bounded variables have finite second moments, m(x)=x² is a continuous genuine CEF. Degree-0 and degree-1 minimizers are the constant 1/3 (symmetry makes Cov(X,Y)=0), and p_J=x² for every J≥2 minimizes prediction risk. Its CEF approximation error is then zero, and its residual risk is 1. Thus the PDF branch is not vacuous; singleton laws also satisfy the literal full-interval PMF branch. The impossibility of nondegenerate real intervals of positive-mass atoms does not remove the nondegenerate PDF case. Not Lean-compiled.
